## TL;DR

Addressed review round 3's contradictory PATH guidance. Native validation's
health probe and configured project command use `bash -lc`, which is a
non-interactive login shell. Updated the operator guide and QA note to say so,
and strengthened the documentation regression test to check both the documented
behavior and the maintained native runner script. The single successful
changed-path check used `--local-tests`; no runner was contacted in this turn.

## Work and rationale

The review identified two different remote command contexts being described as
if they were the same. The engineer-session setup checklist asks operators to
make CLI binaries available to a plain non-login SSH command. Native validation
uses a different path: `prereqProbeCommand` runs its native tool probe through
`bash -lc`, and `scripts/remote-runner/validate-macos.sh` runs a configured
project command the same way. That means the validation command gets the SSH
user's non-interactive login-shell environment. The prior `login environment`
and `non-login SSH environment` statements in the runner setup section
contradicted each other.

I updated `docs/remote-validation.md` to name `bash -lc` explicitly for both
the native project command and native tool probe, and to tell operators that
tools must be available in that user's login PATH. I clarified that
interactive-only startup files are not read by a non-interactive login shell.
The separate engineer CLI checklist still describes non-login SSH PATH
behavior, which is a distinct workflow and remains accurate.

The regression test now reads `validate-macos.sh`, checks the documented
`bash -lc` execution mode, and checks that the script itself uses that shell
form. The QA record now describes native non-interactive login-shell PATH
behavior instead of saying non-login PATH. No application UI code changed in
this follow-up.

## Approaches tried

I read the latest review, searched runner documentation and tests for login,
non-login and PATH guidance, then inspected `prereqProbeCommand` and the native
runner script. This source comparison established the behavior without
connecting to any runner. I fixed the stale description to match the code and
left the unrelated engineer-session CLI guidance unchanged.

## Challenges and blockers

The earlier review also repeats an already-recorded finding: a prior session's
default `repoos check` initiated an SSH link probe to `nick@thinkpad`, which
violated the task's read-only requirement. That historic interaction cannot be
undone. The QA note remains candid about it and records that its payload went
to `/dev/null`; this follow-up made no SSH connection, ran no setup recipe and
changed no runner. To respect the no-SSH requirement, this turn's check used
`REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check --local-tests`.

The first check attempt found a formatting issue in the new test and stopped
before running tests. I ran the repository formatter, then reran the scoped
check. The final run passed formatting, lint, build, UI audits, all scoped
tests, headless UI smoke and the user-docs build. The live users, PATH and
installed tools on bee, thinkpad and mini remain unverified.

## Key learnings

`bash -lc` means a non-interactive login shell: login startup files and login
PATH setup apply, while interactive-only shell configuration does not. Runner
documentation must distinguish that native validation context from a plain
non-login SSH command used to verify engineer CLI availability. Code inspection
was sufficient to settle this distinction; live runner access was neither
needed nor used.
